question: Does the older official INT8QK/FP16PV Triton component path actually compile and match its chosen quantized reference on this4090, and what are full-preparation versus prepared-K/V whole-call costs relative to FA2 at known video shapes?
is_not: No new algorithm, no revival of QVG decoder reuse, no same-codec comparison against QVG PRQ, no SOTA/quality/new methodology claim.
arms: official older Triton modules via explicit full-preparation pad/mask pipeline
same pipeline with K/V prepared once and Q freshly quantized each call

small_tests.reference: Saved INT8 codes/scales dequantized with CPUFP64 softmax (base2 scales times ln2) and FP16 V; whole versus prepared output bytes must match.
small_tests.gates_meaning: Numerical implementation sanity versus same quantized representation; not BF16/video-quality thresholds.
small_tests.failure: Any small-case failure stops before all large timing.

large_shapes.dtype: BF16 raw inputs; FP16V within Sage1 path
large_shapes.mask: noncausal valid K plus explicit zero-padding and broadcast boolean padding mask
large_shapes.crossed_order: three-arm cyclic order, identical per-cycle Q fixture (alternating two fresh fixed Q tensors), static K/V only reused

source: Pinned original math modules unchanged; private import adapter. Source JIT decorators CPU imported, no C++ extension needed.

runtime_limits_proposal.GPU_JIT: Triton compile only during authorized runtime, first-use compile cost recorded separately and included in total cap

preservation: Save small-case codes/scales/V/outputs for separate CPU arithmetic audit, large-case scalar errors/timings/byte digests/counters only. No enormous score matrix or full large QKV artifact.
forbid: Claim numerical match to BF16 or total video speedup from this synthetic probe
